assertion.statement: The irreducible rational cubic H in the degree-obstruction argument is geometrically integral.
assertion.objects: The homogenized cubic H with forms X0,X1 and rational zeros of inputs0 and1.
assertion.hypotheses: H is irreducible over Q of degree3, has the two specified rational zeros, and every rational zero on X0=1 has integer input.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: The input is X1/X0; the two zeros are normalized by X0=1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: If geometrically reducible, irreducibility over Q makes the geometric factors one Galois orbit. Characteristic zero excludes repetition, so degree3 forces three conjugate linear factors. Every rational zero lies on all three; the rational line joining the two specified zeros remains in their intersection and realizes every rational input, contradiction.

assertion.statement: A nonconstant rational function on a nonempty rational affine open cannot take only integer values on its rational points.
assertion.objects: The composite of X1/X0 with the dominant rational parametrization of the actual quotient cubic.
assertion.hypotheses: The parametrization is dominant over Q; its domain meets the input chart in a nonempty open; X1/X0 is nonconstant.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: Shrink to a rational affine principal open avoiding the denominator. No density of rational points on the cubic itself is assumed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
assertion.limit_order: Dominance preserves nonconstancy in function fields. Choose a real ball in the affine principal open. Rational density and continuity put its whole image in the closed set Z; connectedness makes that image constant. The numerator minus this constant times the denominator vanishes on a real open ball, hence identically, contradiction.

assertion.statement: For the specified q0,q1 and J, J^2 q_i have nonnegative valuation at each vertical generic point of the maximal stack.
assertion.objects: The actual t=32s, four branch values a_i, q0=(dt)^2/product(t-a_i), q1=tq0, and J=product p^delta_p.
assertion.hypotheses: The maximal stack is semistable and regular; at a vertical generic point p is a uniformizer and the relative differential kills p. The displayed forms and delta_p use the fixed branch values.
assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
assertion.parameter_range: The actual discriminant210 maximal stack and all vertical generic points.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
assertion.constants: The same J=2765952000 and delta_p; no new height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Work on the maximal stack, with ordinary p-adic valuations; no integral coarse pullback is used.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Codimension-two extension and archimedean metric comparison remain separate.
assertion.limit_order: Write r_i=v(t-a_i). Since d(p)=0, v(dt)>=max r_i. If v(t)<0 all r_i agree and both forms have nonnegative valuation. Otherwise at most one r_i exceeds delta_p and 2max r_i-sum r_i>=-2delta_p. Multiplication by J^2 cancels this possible pole. Extension across codimension2 is a distinct retained input, not a conclusion of this valuation calculation.
